title: USB 3.2 spec (Rev 1.1) -- full LTSSM 12-state machine, substates, timeout table, and USB3-only transfer/descriptor additions
summary: Deep extraction of D:\DV\Task\USB\DOC\USB 3.2 Revision 1.1.pdf, citations by pdftotext -layout line number in .work\pdftxt\usb32.txt (30768 lines). Uses 'Enhanced SuperSpeed' (eSS) naming convention throughout. LTSSM (sec 7.5, p.159+, lines 10396-13100+): 12 states grouped by function -- OPERATIONAL(4): U0 (link active, packets flow or idle; sec 7.5.6 p.189-190, lines 12160-12296 -- has tU0RecoveryTimeout 1ms timer resetting on every received link command, tU0LTimeout 10us keepalive timer triggering single LDN(downstream)/LUP(upstream) on expiry, HP response-time budget tDHPResponse is speed/lane-dependent: Gen1x1<2540ns/Gen2x1<1610ns/Gen1x2<2270ns/Gen2x2<1355ns; exits to Recovery on any sec-7.3 error or TS1-OS detection or 1ms no-link-command timeout, to eSS.Inactive after 3 consecutive failed U3-entry attempts or 4 consecutive PENDING_HP_TIMER timeouts, to Rx.Detect on Warm Reset; requires Port Capability LMP exchange within tPortConfiguration after every U0 entry path or ports get directed to eSS.Inactive/eSS.Disabled), U1 (low-power, PHY may power down, sec 7.5.7), U2 (deeper low-power than U1, higher exit latency, sec 7.5.8), U3 (link suspend, most aggressive power saving, sec 7.5.9). INIT/TRAINING(4): Rx.Detect (power-on link-partner detection, sec 7.5.3), Polling (Tx/Rx training+sync, sec 7.5.4 -- HAS 8 SUBSTATES: Polling.LFPS, Polling.LFPSPlus, Polling.PortMatch, Polling.PortConfig, Polling.RxEQ, Polling.Active, Polling.Configuration, Polling.Idle -- line 10883-10899), Recovery (retrain link on low-power exit, U0 error, or mode switch; sec 7.5.10 p.195 lines 12512-820 -- HAS 3 SUBSTATES: Recovery.Active/Configuration/Idle; unlike Polling does NOT retrain receiver equalizer, only exchanges TS1/TS2 OS to resync; Recovery.Active->Configuration requires 8 consecutive identical TS1-or-TS2 OS received on each lane, Gen2 excludes symbols14/15 which carry DC-balance variation only), Hot Reset (downstream resets upstream, sec 7.5.12 p.203 lines 12963-13030 -- HAS 2 SUBSTATES: Active/Exit; sequence: downstream sends>=16 TS2-OS with Reset bit asserted->upstream echoes asserted->upstream de-asserts on completion->downstream echoes de-asserted->both exit to Hot Reset.Exit->idle-symbol handshake->both return to U0; resets Link Error Count and PM/U1/U2 timers to zero but explicitly PRESERVES port Configuration information unchanged, unlike a cold/Warm reset). TEST(2): Loopback (bit-error test, sec 7.5.11), Compliance Mode (transmitter voltage/timing test, sec 7.5.5, NO substates, disabled-by-default for downstream ports to prevent bad-device auto-entry). ERROR/DISABLED(2): eSS.Inactive (link error, needs SW intervention), eSS.Disabled (eSS connectivity off, may fall back to USB2). U0/U1/U2/U3/Compliance Mode are explicitly flat (no substates). TIMEOUT TABLE (Table 7-12, lines 10447-10484) -- full set of real numeric LTSSM timers a checker/monitor needs, e.g.: teSSInactiveQuietTimeout=12ms, tRxDetectQuietTimeoutDFP=12-120ms, tPollingLFPSTimeout=360ms, tPollingSCDLFPSTimeout(SSP)=60us, tPollingActiveTimeout=12ms(x1)/24ms(x2), tPollingIdleTimeout=2ms, tU0RecoveryTimeout=1ms, tU0LTimeout=10us, tNoLFPSResponseTimeout(U1)=2ms, tU1PingTimeout=300ms, tNoLFPSResponseTimeout(U3)=300ms, tRecoveryActiveTimeout=2ms, tRecoveryConfigurationTimeout=10ms, tRecoveryIdleTimeout=12ms, tLoopbackExitTimeout=6ms, tHotResetActiveTimeout=2ms, tHotResetExitTimeout=2ms, tU3WakeupRetryDelay=12ms, tU2RxdetDelay=2ms, tU3RxdetDelay=100ms. CAVEAT: the pdftotext -layout extraction has misaligned columns around the PORT_U2_TIMEOUT/tU1PingTimeout/tNoLFPSResponseTimeout(U2) rows -- verify against the actual PDF page image (~p.161) before hard-coding those three specific values into a checker. NAMING RISK FLAGGED (unverified, no older-spec text locally to compare): this Rev 1.1 spec uses eSS.Disabled/eSS.Inactive; if any local VIP/RTL was built against older USB3.0/3.1-era spec text it may use bare SS.Disabled/SS.Inactive naming instead -- check actual VIP source strings before assuming exact match. USB3-ONLY TRANSFER-TYPE ADDITIONS (sec 4.4, p.41-43, lines 4069-4168): Bulk Streams (4.4.6.4) -- extends single-FIFO bulk pipe to a multi-stream model via Stream Protocol; each Stream gets a Stream ID (SID); handshake is device ERDY tagged with CStream ID -> host issues IN ACK TPs tagged with that CStream ID -> device returns DPs tagged with CStream ID; extends host buffer count per bulk endpoint from 1 to up to 65533 (1:1 SID-to-buffer mapping); either host or device may initiate/reject stream selection; an error still halts the whole pipe (same halt semantics as plain USB2 bulk) even though many logical streams are multiplexed onto it. Isochronous/Interrupt in USB3.2 explicitly extend rather than replace the USB2 model (spec text cross-references back to USB2 sec 5.7 directly). USB3.2 DESCRIPTORS (sec 9.6, lines 20321-21717): adds on top of (not replacing) USB2's device/config/interface/endpoint descriptors. BOS (Binary Device Object Store, sec 9.6.2) is a container for device-capability sub-descriptors: USB2.0 Extension, SuperSpeed USB Device Capability, Container ID, Platform Descriptor, SuperSpeedPlus USB Device Capability, Precision Time Measurement, Configuration Summary Descriptor, FWStatus Capability (headers located, not all individually deep-read this pass). SuperSpeed Endpoint Companion (Table 9-28, sec 9.6.7, lines 21548-21668, DEEP-READ) -- 6-byte descriptor immediately following every non-EP0 endpoint descriptor at SuperSpeed+: bMaxBurst(0-15, burst of 1-16 packets, MUST be 0 for control endpoints); bmAttributes meaning depends on transfer type (mirrors USB2's one-field-many-meanings pattern) -- Bulk: bits4:0=MaxStreams (0=none, 1-16 encodes 2^MaxStreams streams); Control/Interrupt: reserved=0; Isochronous: bits1:0=Mult (max packets/SI = (bMaxBurst+1)x(Mult+1), max value 2), bit7=SSP-ISO-Companion flag meaning an SSP Iso EP Companion descriptor immediately follows; wBytesPerInterval = total bytes/service-interval for periodic endpoints only, must be zero for control/bulk. SuperSpeedPlus Isochronous Endpoint Companion (sec 9.6.8) only valid above Gen1 speed and only for iso endpoints needing >48K bytes/SI (header-level only this pass).
